llm_text: One approach that’s worked for me is pairing a referral with a reliable “station buddy” for the first 2–3 weeks so they can shadow during service and get real-time coaching. I set small, concrete goals (ticket times, one new station competency, handling guest interactions) and do quick end-of-week check-ins to praise progress and address problems. Rotate them through stations until they’re competent, then give incremental responsibility and public recognition so they feel ownership. Consistent expectations (attendance, attitude) and modeling calm under pressure, plus mentoring on soft skills like communication and handling complaints, really turns a new hire into a dependable long-term team member.
